correctness.rationale: For fixed d≥2, 2≤q<∞, a>0 and p≥0, take a unit dual functional u with unit norming point v. For a unit x, putting δ=1−u·x in Clarkson gives ||x−v||_q^q/2^q ≤ 1−(1−δ/2)^q ≤ qδ/2. Scaling by r=||k||_q and comparing norms yields the claimed lower bound c r^(1−q)dist₂(k,R₊v)^q. In a shell L≤r<2L the ray tube of radius W intersects a Euclidean ball of radius O(L); the unit cubes centered at the lattice points fit in the thickened tube of length O(L+W+1), giving O((L+W+1)(W+1)^(d−1)) uniformly in direction. With W₀=L^(1−1/q), the innermost tube counts O(L^p_c) and successive annuli are exponentially damped in (W/W₀)^q. This gives uniform summability of the tilted polynomial weight for p>p_c. For n≠0 use its norming functional to minorize the triangle defect by either endpoint's tilt defect; the triangle inequality and (A+B)^p≤2^(p−1)(A^p+B^p) bound the polynomial quotient by the two endpoint weights. The n=0 sum converges directly. Axially, for s>0 the transverse defect is comparable to min(||z||_q^q/s^(q−1),||z||_q), by the mean-value theorem for ||z||_q≤s and rescaling by ||z||_q otherwise; at s=0 it is exactly ||z||_q. Its exponential sum is O((1+s)^α) by lattice balls and annuli, α=(d−1)(1−1/q). For 0≤m≤N/2 this leaves O((1+m)^(α−p)) per layer; beyond [0,N] the additional 2·dist(m,[0,N]) and polynomial quotient ≤1 yield O(1) total. Boxes of transverse radius proportional to m^(1−1/q) give the matching lower sums for 1≤m≤N/4 at criticality, or m comparable to N on a central interval below criticality. Finally, on m≤N/2 the summands converge pointwise to the axial tilt (since ||Ne₁−k||_q−(N−k₁) tends to zero) and are dominated by 2^p times that summable tilt. The reflected half gives the other copy, and a possible midpoint layer tends to zero by domination. This proves the claimed orders, necessity and exact limit.
residual_risks: The NumPy checker compares finite truncated sums, not the uniform angular estimate, exact limit, or sharp asymptotic constants; correctness rests on the analytic bounds and convergence argument.

value.rationale: This turns a useful Fourier Hilbert-algebra hypothesis into an exact test across a natural anisotropic family. It identifies the axes as witnesses to failure of the uniform estimate, resolves the borderline logarithm, and gives an exact supercritical normalization beyond the threshold decision. The argument explains why norm equivalence does not preserve the exponent and why the transverse geometry matters.
residual_risks: No necessity claim for all possible algebra proofs, no sharp global constant or critical leading coefficient, and no uniformity in q tending to infinity.
